record.original_question: Let f run over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f <= T. Prove asymptotic formulas, with the best possible error terms, for the third and fourth moments of the central values L(1/2, f), normalized by L(1, ad f), in particular aiming for sums of the shape T^2 P3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) for the cubic moment and T^2 P6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)) for the quartic moment.

evidence.quote: Prove third and fourth moment asymptotics with best possible error terms for L(1/2, f ) as f runs over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight kf <= T. It should be possible to show, using current technology, that ... = T^2 P3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) and ... = T^2 P6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an even integer k ≥ 2, let H_k denote the set of normalized holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k for the full modular group SL_2(Z). For f ∈ H_k, let L(s, f) denote the associated Hecke L-function, normalized so that the functional equation relates s to 1 − s and the central point is s = 1/2. Let L(s, ad f) denote the adjoint (symmetric square) L-function of f, and consider the harmonic-type weight 1/L(1, ad f). For a parameter T → ∞, consider the cubic and quartic moments

   M_3(T) = Σ_{k ≤ T, k even} Σ_{f ∈ H_k} (Γ(k−1)/(4π)^{k−1}) · L(1/2, f)^3 / L(1, ad f),
   M_4(T) = Σ_{k ≤ T, k even} Σ_{f ∈ H_k} (Γ(k−1)/(4π)^{k−1}) · L(1/2, f)^4 / L(1, ad f).

Prove asymptotic formulas with the strongest possible error terms. In particular, establish that there exist polynomials P_3 of degree 3 and P_6 of degree 6 such that, for every ε > 0,

   M_3(T) = T^2 P_3(log T) + O_ε(T^{1+ε}),
   M_4(T) = T^2 P_6(log T) + O_ε(T^{4/3+ε}),

and determine the leading coefficients of P_3 and P_6 explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: No published asymptotic with the requested power-saving error term T^{1+ε} for the cubic moment or T^{4/3+ε} for the quartic moment over weights k ≤ T of holomorphic Hecke eigenforms is known. Existing results give asymptotics for the fourth moment only up to a power saving in the weight under restrictive conditions (e.g., dyadic ranges or under GLH/GRH), and an unconditional asymptotic for holomorphic forms at this precision is regarded as substantially harder than the analogous problem for Maass forms. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms
status_evidence.snippet: The fourth moment of holomorphic Hecke cusp forms is bounded by a constant provided that the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis holds.
status_evidence.claim: Unconditional asymptotic for the fourth moment with power-saving error is not established; only bounds under GRH are known.

status_evidence.title: On the fourth moment of Hecke Maass forms and the Random Wave Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Proving an asymptotic for the fourth moment in [the holomorphic] case, on GLH or any other reasonable hypothesis, seems to be much harder than the problem for Maass forms.
status_evidence.claim: The fourth moment asymptotic for holomorphic Hecke eigenforms remains open.
